images.caption: The Three Bridges at Devil's Bridge. In the area surrounding the falls, the natural world flourishes in abundance. The woodland is dominated by mature oak and beech trees intermingled with silver birch, their gnarled branches draped with a rich layer of mosses and lichens. On the forest floor, clusters of ferns, wild garlic and bluebells emerge in spring, while hardy heathers and bilberry add splashes of colour across the rocky outcrops during the drier months. The site teems with wildlife; birds such as woodpeckers, nuthatches and kingfishers are frequent visitors to the cascading water, and small mammals like red squirrels can sometimes be seen flitting among the trees. This blend of rugged geological features, rich vegetation and diverse fauna creates a vibrant, living tableau that captures the essence of rural Wales.

description: This walk takes you from the Ceredigion Coast at Borth to the wonderful waterfall at Devil's Bridge Falls near Aberystwyth. The trail runs for about 16.5 miles following waymarked footpaths through the region. Along the way you will pass a series of pretty reservoirs and some historic old mining sites while enjoying splendid views of the surrounding countryside. You will also visit the neighbouring village of Talybont which is a nice place to stop for refreshments.
